resource: PubMed (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) — bibliographic
applicability: Fully applicable: PubMed indexes the oligonucleotide coagulation-toxicity literature end to end, from 1990s phosphorothioate in-vitro mechanism work in human plasma through current phase 3 trial reports, and NCBI E-utilities gave unrestricted programmatic access.
notes: RESOURCE PERFORMANCE: PubMed via NCBI E-utilities (esearch.fcgi + efetch.fcgi, JSON and XML) worked without authentication, rate-limiting or CAPTCHA across 31 queries. No barrier for the resource itself. I used the API throughout and never scraped the web UI, per the hard rules.  ONE METHOD CORRECTION WORTH FLAGGING: my first efetch parser used an XPath of './/ArticleIdList/ArticleId', which also matches ArticleIdList elements nested inside each record's ReferenceList, so early output attached reference DOIs/PMCIDs to the wrong parent article (e.g. PMID 38563414 initially showed a spurious PMC7249474 and a Bioanalysis DOI). Fixed by anchoring to 'PubmedData/ArticleIdList'. Every identifier in the results above was re-verified against Europe PMC's core record, so the DOIs/PMCIDs reported are correct. If the parent agent is running similar parses on PubMed XML, this is a live trap.  ACCESS

barrier: The Europe PMC REST API itself was fully usable - no login wall, CAPTCHA, rate limit or API error at any point across 24 queries. The search endpoint, resultType=core retrieval and the fullTextXML endpoint all returned results, and I read OA full text for three records (PMC9718591, PMC13009829, PMC13083634-adjacent checks). Barriers were per-record retrieval blocks only, recorded exactly: (1) Sheehan & Lan, Blood 1998, PMID 9716589 - Europe PMC fullTextUrlList advertises 'Free after 12 months | html | http://www.bloodjournal.org/cgi/content/full/92/5/1617'; following https://doi.org/10.1182/blood.v92.5.1617 redirected to https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/92/5/1617/247353/Phosphorothioate-Oligonucleotides-Inhibit-the and returned HTTP 403. No PMC record, no author manuscript, no preprint. Abstract free only. resource: OpenAlex (https://openalex.org/) — bibliographic, open REST API (api.openalex.org)
barrier: PARTIAL BARRIER, resource still searched. OpenAlex now meters its API by credit budget. Every list/search call (/works?search=, /works?filter=) costs 10 credits / $0.001 and the shared-IP free daily budget was already at zero on arrival: "Rate limit exceeded ... Insufficient budget. This request has no API key, so it counts against the free daily budget shared by everyone on your network's IP address, and that budget is used up ($0 remaining; resets at midnight UTC)". HTTP 429, retry-after 74121s then 73668s (~20.5h), x-ratelimit-remaining: 0, x-ratelimit-remaining-usd: 0, x-ratelimit-onetime-remaining: 0. No OpenAlex API key is configured in this environment and I did not create one (hard rule: no credentials/sign-ups). Verified this was NOT a proxy fault: curl "$HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status" returned enabled, bundleCoversEveryHost true, recentRelayFailures empty. Workaround found and used: single-entity GETs (/works/{openalex_id}, /works/doi:{doi}) and /autocomplete/works return HTTP 200 at x-ratelimit-credits-used: 0, i.e. they are not metered. I therefore ran the bulk of the search on that zero-cost surface (~43 autocomplete/title probes plus ~165 single-work GETs doing a referenced_works/related_works citation walk from 5 seed papers). Of 13 attempted metered list queries, 2 succeeded (the aPTT query, 189 hits; the contact-activation/FXII/prekallikrein query, 13 hits) because the budget trickles; 11 were refused. A background job retried 6 of the blocked queries 14 ti
applicability: Highly applicable as a discovery and open-access-routing layer: OpenAlex indexes the entire oligonucleotide coagulation literature and its per-work "locations" array is the single most useful field here, because it reveals legal green/bronze copies (PMC, Amsterdam UMC Pure, institutional repositories) for papers whose publisher version is paywalled. Its limitation for this endpoint is that it carries only titles, abstracts and metadata - it holds no sequence tables, no per-position chemistry, no purity certificates and no assay-level measurements, so it can locate and triage gap-3 and gap-4 evidence but can never itself close those gaps; the supplementary files must be pulled from the resolved full-text host.
notes: RANKING BASIS: ordered by the Phase 2 criteria (human in vitro system first, then human/animal extrapolability, then sequence and per-position chemistry, then purity), not by row volume. Results 1-3 and 9 are human in vitro/ex vivo (gap 1); 4, 6, 7 are same-construct or same-class cross-species bridges (gap 2); 8 is the best sequence-and-modification panel (gap 3); 12 is the only purity reference found (gap 4); 5, 10, 11 are named acquisition targets (gap 5).  GAP-5 SCORECARD. (a) ATLAS-A/B NCT03417245 primary publication: LOCATED (W4361195612, DOI 10.1016/S2352-3026(23)00037-6, PMID 37003278) but NOT OBTAINED - closed at Lancet Haematol, and the only green deposit is 401-walled at Southampton. Useful consolation prize: three sibling fitusiran phase 3 reports ARE free and were verified open in this session - ATLAS-PPX (W4392543341, PMC11181353, and its supplementary appendix is deposited

resource: Semantic Scholar (https://www.semanticscholar.org/) — Graph API v1, unauthenticated (api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1)
barrier: PARTIAL BARRIER — HTTP 429 rate limiting on the unauthenticated Semantic Scholar Graph API shared pool. Exact response body, returned on the very first request and repeatedly thereafter: {"message": "Too Many Requests. Please wait and try again or apply for a key for higher rate limits. https://www.semanticscholar.org/product/api#api-key-form", "code": "429"}. Mitigation applied: single-threaded requests, 3-6 s spacing between calls, and exponential backoff of up to 14 retries per request (7 s rising to 46 s, ~370 s total per request). Six requests still completed and returned data (4 /paper/search calls and 2 /paper/{id}/citations calls, read in full). Eleven further search requests exhausted all 14 retries without ever receiving a 200 and are recorded above as ATTEMPTED, NO RESULTS — they were NOT searched. The named targets for mipomersen (ISIS 301012-CS5 / CS7 RADICHOL II / CS12) and donidalorsen were lost to this and remain unsearched on this resource. No API key was obtained (would require registration/credentials, which the task forbids). Separate, smaller barrier: the /paper/{id}/citations and /references endpoints reject the field "authors.name" with {"error": "Unrecognized or unsupported fields: [authors.name]"} — valid on /paper/search but not on the graph endpoints; this cost one attempt at the FXI-ASO /references list, which was then dropped in favour of the two /citations calls to conserve rate-limit budget. No login wall, no CAPTCHA, no browser check was encoun
applicability: Applicable, but only as a discovery layer: Semantic Scholar is purely bibliographic, so it can find and open-route papers but holds no supplementary files, sequence tables, modification maps or certificates of analysis itself — gaps 3 (per-position chemistry) and 4 (purity/characterisation) cannot be closed here, only pointed at.
notes: WHAT THIS RESOURCE IS ACTUALLY GOOD FOR HERE. Keyword relevance search was poor: generic coagulation queries returned mostly off-target records (seaweed sulfated polysaccharides, FXIa small molecules, plasma freezing stability) because the ranker keys on the coagulation vocabulary and ignores the oligonucleotide constraint. The productive mode was the CITATION GRAPH. One call to /paper/DOI:10.1089/oli.1.1997.7.503/citations?limit=100 — forward citations of the 1997 phosphorothioate/coagulation paper — yielded four of the five human in vitro records in this list, including both Sheehan intrinsic-tenase papers that keyword search never surfaced. A second call on the FXI-ASO cynomolgus paper yielded the human/animal bridge pairs. RECOMMENDATION for the remaining 429-blocked ground: do not re-run keyword searches here; instead run /citations and /references on the seeds this sweep establishe

barrier: Two-layer barrier, affecting FILE DOWNLOADS ONLY — the search API and all dataset/file metadata were fully readable, so this resource counts as genuinely searched. (1) API download route requires auth: GET https://datadryad.org/api/v2/files/73804/download returns HTTP/2 401 with body {"error":"Unauthorized, must have current bearer token"} (56 bytes); same 401 for the dataset-level route /api/v2/datasets/doi%3A10.5061%2Fdryad.dh250/download. (2) The public route advertised on the landing page, https://datadryad.org/downloads/file_stream/73804, returns HTTP 403 (nginx plain-HTML 403, 118 bytes) with a default user agent; with a browser user agent plus Referer it returns HTTP 200 but serves an Anubis proof-of-work browser-validation interstitial instead of the file (<title>Validating...</title>, stylesheet /.within.website/x/xess/xess.min.css, 4324 bytes) — a browser check I did not attempt to defeat. Legal open alternative route tried and failed: the primary article is NOT open access and NOT in PMC (Europe PMC core record for DOI 10.1093/toxsci/kfx118: isOpenAccess=N, inPMC=N, pmcid=null), so the Oxford-hosted supplementary tables are paywalled too. Net effect: I can name and describe the AYX1 files from their curator descriptions but cannot read their contents from this environment. No purchases, credentials or author contact were used.
applicability: Dryad applies in principle (it is a general-purpose repository that does hold both oligonucleotide studies and human coagulation studies) but in practice its holdings on this specific intersection are essentially empty: the oligonucleotide result set and the coagulation result set are completely disjoint, with exactly one oligonucleotide toxicology deposit and zero datasets in which an oligonucleotide is tested in any human coagulation system.
